description:

title: Physical Therapist (PT) – Mobile/Home-Based Care
description:
Overview

We are seeking a skilled, compassionate, and dependable Physical Therapist (PT) to provide high-quality physical therapy services to patients in their homes throughout the Fresno region.

The Physical Therapist will travel to patients' homes to perform comprehensive evaluations, develop individualized plans of care, provide skilled therapeutic interventions, monitor patient progress, and educate patients and caregivers on strategies to improve mobility, function, safety, and independence.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently in a home-based environment, has strong clinical judgment and communication skills, and is passionate about delivering patient-centered care.

This is a 1099 independent contractor position.

Duties and Responsibilities

· Travel to patients' homes throughout the assigned service area to provide physical therapy services.

· Perform comprehensive physical therapy evaluations in the patient's home environment.

· Assess strength, range of motion, balance, gait, mobility, coordination, endurance, pain, functional limitations, and ability to safely perform activities of daily living.

· Evaluate the patient's home environment and identify potential safety and fall risks that may impact mobility and independence.

· Develop individualized plans of care based on evaluation findings, physician orders/referrals, patient needs, clinical judgment, and functional goals.

· Establish measurable short-term and long-term functional goals.

· Provide skilled physical therapy interventions appropriate to the patient's diagnosis and functional limitations, including:

o Therapeutic exercises

o Therapeutic activities

o Neuromuscular re-education

o Gait and mobility training

o Balance and coordination training

o Functional strengthening

o Manual therapy when clinically appropriate

o Transfer training

o Fall prevention and safety training

· Train patients in the safe use of assistive devices such as walkers, canes, and other mobility equipment.

· Develop and instruct patients in individualized home exercise programs.

· Educate patients and caregivers regarding diagnosis, treatment, exercises, mobility, safety, fall prevention, and strategies to promote independence.

· Monitor patient response to treatment and make appropriate clinical modifications to the plan of care.

· Perform reassessments and communicate changes in patient condition or functional status as appropriate.

· Coordinate care with physicians, nurses, caregivers, physical therapist assistants, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals.

· Communicate effectively with referring providers regarding patient progress, concerns, and recommendations.

· Complete accurate, timely, and thorough documentation for evaluations, daily treatment visits, reassessments, progress reports, and discharge summaries.

· Maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations, professional standards, payer requirements, and company policies.

· Recognize changes in patient condition that may require physician notification, additional medical evaluation, or modification of treatment.

· Maintain patient confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.

· Provide compassionate, respectful, and professional care to patients and their families in the home setting.

Requirements

· Current and valid California Physical Therapist license in good standing.

· Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapy program.

· Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, and rehabilitation principles.

· Strong clinical reasoning and patient assessment skills.

· Ability to independently perform comprehensive PT evaluations and develop appropriate plans of care.

· Experience treating patients with orthopedic, musculoskeletal, neurological, balance, gait, weakness, mobility, and/or functional limitations preferred.

· Strong knowledge of therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, functional mobility, neuromuscular re-education, and fall prevention.

· Excellent patient assessment and acute/chronic pain management skills.

· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

· Ability to work independently and effectively manage a mobile patient caseload.

· Must be punctual, dependable, organized, and professional.

· Comfortable entering and providing care in patients' homes and working with patients and caregivers in a home-based environment.

· Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.

· Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.

· CPR/BLS certification preferred or required according to company policy.

· Previous home health, mobile therapy, outpatient, orthopedic, neurological, geriatric, or community-based experience is preferred.

Mobile/Home-Based Care Expectations

Because this position involves providing care in patients' homes, the Physical Therapist must be able to:

· Arrive at scheduled visits within the expected timeframe.

· Manage travel time and maintain an efficient daily schedule.

· Carry and transport necessary clinical equipment and supplies.

· Adapt treatment approaches to different home environments and available space.

· Maintain a safe and professional environment during every patient visit.

· Communicate promptly regarding cancellations, scheduling changes, or patient concerns.

· Respect patients' homes, privacy, routines, and individual preferences.

· Demonstrate sound clinical judgment when working independently in the community.

Documentation and Compliance

The Physical Therapist is responsible for completing all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timeframes, including:

· Initial evaluations

· Treatment notes

· Reassessments

· Progress reports

· Recertifications, when applicable

· Discharge documentation

· Home exercise programs

· Communication with referring providers

· Other documentation required by the organization, payer, or applicable regulations

Job Type

Full-time – 1099 Independent Contractor

Pay Structure (1099)

· Guaranteed base pay: $1,080 per week

· Base compensation is calculated at $45 per patient visit, based on a minimum of 6 patient visits per day.

· $45 per additional patient visit for visits beyond the daily base of 6.

· Compensation is subject to the terms of the independent contractor agreement.

Schedule

4/10 Schedule

· Four 10-hour workdays per week

· Typical start time: 7:30 AM–8:30 AM, depending on patient scheduling and geographic coverage.

· Daily schedule may vary based on patient locations, visit duration, and patient needs.

Work Location

Mobile/Home-Based – Fresno Region

The Physical Therapist will travel to assigned patients' homes throughout the designated service area.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a clinically confident, compassionate, and self-motivated Physical Therapist who enjoys working one-on-one with patients and families. The successful candidate will be comfortable making clinical decisions independently, adapting treatment to the patient's home environment, and providing high-quality care while maintaining excellent documentation and communication.

This position is an excellent opportunity for a Physical Therapist who values autonomy, flexibility, meaningful patient relationships, and community-based care

title: Utilities Engineer
description:
PACIV, a global leader in industrial automation solutions with offices in Ireland, the United States and Puerto Rico, and serving the Life Science, Food & Beverage (F&B) and Utilities industries, is looking for an experienced Utilities Engineer for a F&B project. This is a site-based role.
The Utilities Engineer will be responsible for the implementation of all utilities systems, which are to be delivered safely, on time, in full and meet the stringent requirements of F&B production environments.
The role will support the design, installation, commissioning, and handover of various site utilities including HVAC systems, Compressed Air, Cooling & Steam systems, Nitrogen Generation & Storage systems, Heat Recovery & Energy optimizations systems and Waste Water Treatment Plant.
Work closely with the internal cross functional project team, EPCM partners, suppliers, and OEMs to ensure hygiene zoning, environmental control, driving energy efficiency initiatives, and regulatory compliance across the facility.


Responsibilities of the Role

Utilities Ownership
  • Act as the technical owner for Utilities requirements.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert (SME) for all Utilities requirements onsite .

Project Engineering
  • Lead and support utility related project of greenfield utility installations.
  • Support Utility installation, integration, commissioning and qualification (IQ, OQ & PQ).
  • Manage contractors on site to ensure on time in full milestones.
  • Support FAT/SAT, performance testing, and final environmental qualifications.
  • Troubleshoot utility performance issues during construction, commissioning, and startup.

CAPEX
  • Support Utility CAPEX package scope, planning, and reporting.
  • Provide technical input and support into cost/forecast accuracy, schedule adherence, and risk registers.
  • Support change control and ensure all Utility changes are fully assessed and documented.

Collaboration
  • Work closely with Quality, Operations, EHS, R&I, Maintenance and Engineering to ensure utilities meet environmental and hygienic requirements.
  • Collaborate with EPCM partners, Utility consultants and existing site team on utility operations, assess availability, generation, manage tie‑ins, layout conflicts, and commissioning plans.
  • Support Utility and Automation teams on interdependent systems (BMS, SCADA, EMS).

Procurement & Supplier Management
  • Support technical aspects of tenders for utility systems (URS, RFQ, technical bid evaluations, clarifications).
  • Partner with Regional Engineering and C&P (CAPEX Procurement) for supplier selection and contract alignment.
  • Support OEM/vendor deliverables for documentation, training, spare parts, and commissioning.

Standards, Compliance & Safety
  • Support compliance with Company Engineering Standards; GMP/HACCP and hygiene zoning rules; Cleanroom and environmental control guidelines; Local/European regulations & industry standards.
  • Embed Safety principles in Design & execution during installation and commissioning.

Operational Readiness & Handover
  • Support the development/approval of Utility ‑related SOPs, environmental control procedures, Preventative Maintenance plans, and spare parts lists.
  • Ensure full technical handover to Operations and Maintenance, including training and validated documentation.

Reporting & Decision Support
  • Provide structured updates on utility progress, risks, commissioning readiness, and mitigation plans.
  • Provide technical insights to support strategic and operational decision‑making throughout project phases.


Requirements
Candidates must have a valid EU Work Permit and Irish residency
Please no agencies

Education
  • BSc/BEng in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering or equivalent.
  • Project Management Certification preferred.

Experience & Skills Required
  • 5+ years’ experience in utilities engineering in F&B, pharmaceutical, chemical or related regulated process manufacturing sector.
  • Previous experience in utility delivery in greenfield / brownfield projects.
  • Hands-on experience with multiple utility systems.
  • Experience in energy management and system optimization preferred.
  • Experience collaborating with suppliers, contractors and external engineering firms.
  • Experience with HVAC systems, Building services, Steam & Boilers systems, Chilled Water & refrigeration, Electrical Power Distribution, Compressed Air Systems, Water & Waste Water Treatment Systems.
  • Ability to Interpret drawings, schematics and models.
  • Experience in troubleshooting utility system performance.
  • Familiarity with project management and CAPEX processes.
  • Clear communication with technical and non‑technical stakeholders..
  • Proactive & continuous improvement mindset.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and ability to influence partners and suppliers.
  • Extensive analytical and problem solving abilities in commissioning/start‑up environments.
  • Commitment to Company’s safety and quality culture.

title: Global Head of Operational Excellence & Enablement
description:
About Us
JOLT is a global leader in electric vehicle charging and digital out-of-home media, creating smarter ways for people and brands to move. Operating across the United States, Canada, the U.K., Australia, and New Zealand, JOLT is helping make it faster, easier and simpler for drivers everywhere to switch to electric vehicles. The company combines accessible, reliable EV charging with a digital advertising network that connects brands with consumers at key moments in their daily journeys. By integrating sustainable infrastructure with data-driven media, JOLT delivers measurable impact for advertisers while helping accelerate the shift toward electric mobility worldwide. Recognized by TIME and Statista as one of the world’s top 250 greentech companies, JOLT continues to expand its mission to make charging convenient, accessible, and built for the future.

Lead the design and delivery of JOLT’s AI-first Operations ecosystem — while overseeing Global CX and Supply Chain. This is a role which combines operational leadership with building AI and Automation solutions to operational problems. You will be hands on tools building the Agentic Operations ecosystem for JOLT, collaborating with Digital Product and Software Engineering. You will lead the Global Supply Chain and Customer Experience functions and influence local Operations leads across five markets to drive operational excellence and adopt AI-native ways of working. JOLT operates ~2,600 EV charging/OOH advertising stations across the US, Canada, UK, Australia, and New Zealand. This role is based in the US or Canada.

Operations AI Delivery Lead

  • Own and deliver the AI roadmap for JOLT’s Global Operations — across predictive maintenance, CX automation, and real-time network monitoring

  • Define, prioritise, and ship AI & automation features, translating operational pain points from local Operations Managers into scalable digital product solutions

  • Embed agentic AI workflows across the Operations function, shifting JOLT from reactive to preventative operations

Global CX and Supply Chain

  • Own and lead Global Supply Chain and Customer Experience — setting strategy, leading a small team, owning KPIs, and driving continuous improvement

  • Global Supply Chain at JOLT relates to charging, screen equipment and spare part planning, ordering, storage and transport

  • Global Customer Experience at JOLT relates to driver support via digital and contract centre channels

Local Operational Excellence

  • Drive operational excellence and best practices across global markets by influencing local Operations Managers

  • Own Global Operations & Maintenance Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and operating cadence

  • Drive Continuous Improvement projects across global markets

Required Skills

  • Demonstrated track record of building or owning AI/automation products in an operational context (supply chain, field ops, CX, or logistics)

  • Experience influencing and leading operational teams, ideally in a global context

  • Commercial and analytical mindset: comfortable with data, KPIs, and ROI-based decision making

  • Industry background in EV charging (CPO), physical infrastructure, Out-of-Home Media, or Tech hardware preferred

  • Digital Product management experience a plus

Previous experience

  • 5–10+ years in a blend of Operations and Digital Product or Software Engineering — we are looking for someone who has led operations and built / owned the tools that run them, preferably in EV Charging (CPO), Out-of-Home Media, Tech Hardware or Physical Infrastructure

  • Previous experience in a start-up, scale-up, or consulting environment where you have had to build structure in a fast-paced global environment

To Apply
We're trying to make a difference at JOLT and need entrepreneurial team players who can problem-solve and thrive in ambiguous environments. Even if you don't think you're the perfect fit - that's ok! If you're passionate about what we're doing at JOLT, we want to hear from you!

Our customers come from all backgrounds and it's important that our staff do too. If you think you could add value to our organisation, apply now and let us know why JOLT is the right fit for you.

title: Product Designer (Contract)
description:
B2B Product Designer

Poka Labs · Remote · Part-time, approximately 10–15 hours per week

Poka Labs builds AI agents for chemical and industrial manufacturers. We help commercial teams turn customer requests into quotes, find the right products in large catalogs, and make better pricing decisions.

We’re a YC Summer 2024 company with a small engineering team and a growing product. We’re looking for an experienced contract product designer who can take a complicated workflow, ask the right questions, and turn it into something intuitive that our engineers can build.

We expect an initial engagement of one to two months, with the potential to continue or expand.

The work

Our customers work with tens of thousands of products, complex pricing, and multiple layers of review. We need to make that complexity manageable.

You’ll work directly with our technical co-founder, Andrew, to design new features and improve important workflows across our quoting and pricing products. Examples include:

  • Helping users review AI-recommended price changes across a large product catalog without becoming overwhelmed.
  • Making quote status, review requests, and next steps easy to understand.
  • Showing the reasoning behind AI recommendations at the right level of detail.
  • Incorporating customer feedback while supporting both simple and more complex workflows.

The immediate priority is getting new features and core interactions right. Targeted improvements to the existing product will also be part of the work.

What you’ll own

  • Build enough understanding of our product and customers to make decisions in context.
  • Turn requirements, customer feedback, and conversations into clear user flows and concrete designs.
  • Identify missing requirements, edge cases, and tradeoffs before engineering starts building.
  • Produce implementation-ready screens, prototypes, and concise interaction notes.
  • Work with engineers through implementation and refine designs based on feedback.
  • Establish reusable patterns where they help us build more consistently.

We want to be able to explain what a feature needs to accomplish and trust you to lead the design work, without requiring a founder to direct every screen.

Who we’re looking for

You’re an experienced product designer with strong UX judgment and a track record of making complex software easier to use.

You likely have:

  • Experience designing B2B software with substantial workflows, tables, approvals, or other information-heavy interfaces.
  • The ability to reason through an ambiguous product problem and explain your decisions.
  • Good instincts for hierarchy, progressive disclosure, and helping users understand what to do next.
  • A practical approach to working with a small engineering team: you know where detail matters and when a straightforward solution is enough.
  • The independence to get up to speed, ask focused questions, and move work forward.
  • Comfort using AI tools to explore ideas and accelerate delivery while applying your own design judgment.

Experience with AI products or early-stage startups is helpful. Chemical industry experience isn’t required.

How we’ll work together

This is a hands-on design role with direct access to the founders and engineers. We expect a weekly design touchpoint, with most collaboration happening asynchronously.

We prefer a monthly retainer based on an agreed scope and expected capacity. The starting commitment is approximately 10–15 hours per week, with scope and compensation agreed together. From there we can be more flexible!

title: Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) – Mobile/Home-Based Care
description:
Overview
We are seeking a skilled, compassionate, and dependable Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) to provide high-quality physical therapy services to patients in their homes throughout the San Fernando region.

The Physical Therapist Assistant will work under the direction and supervision of a licensed Physical Therapist to provide skilled therapeutic interventions, implement established plans of care, monitor patient response and progress, reinforce home exercise programs, and educate patients and caregivers on strategies to improve mobility, function, safety, and independence.
The ideal candidate is comfortable working independently within the scope of PTA practice in a home-based environment, has strong communication and interpersonal skills, and is passionate about delivering patient-centered care.
This is a 1099 independent contractor position.

Duties and Responsibilities
  • Travel to patients' homes throughout the assigned service area to provide physical therapy treatment under the direction of the supervising Physical Therapist.
  • Review the patient's established plan of care, treatment goals, precautions, and relevant clinical information prior to providing treatment.
  • Provide skilled physical therapy interventions in accordance with the Physical Therapist's plan of care, including:
    • Therapeutic exercises
    • Therapeutic activities
    • Neuromuscular re-education
    • Gait and mobility training
    • Balance and coordination training
    • Functional strengthening
    • Transfer training
    • Fall prevention and safety training
    • Manual therapy when appropriate and within the PTA's scope of practice
    • Functional mobility and activity training
  • Assist patients with improving strength, range of motion, balance, coordination, endurance, gait, mobility, and functional performance.
  • Train patients in the safe and appropriate use of assistive devices such as walkers, canes, and other mobility equipment as directed by the Physical Therapist.
  • Implement and reinforce individualized home exercise programs established by the Physical Therapist.
  • Educate patients and caregivers regarding prescribed exercises, mobility strategies, safety precautions, fall prevention, positioning, transfers, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Monitor patient response to treatment and recognize changes in pain, functional status, mobility, tolerance, or overall condition.
  • Communicate significant changes in patient condition, response to treatment, progress, concerns, or barriers to the supervising Physical Therapist in a timely manner.
  • Provide feedback to the Physical Therapist regarding patient progress and response to the established plan of care.
  • Assist the Physical Therapist with reassessments and other clinical follow-up activities as appropriate and permitted within the PTA's scope of practice.
  • Modify treatment activities within the established plan of care as appropriate and within the PTA's scope of practice, while communicating clinically significant changes to the supervising Physical Therapist.
  • Reinforce proper body mechanics, transfer techniques, positioning, and safety strategies with patients and caregivers.
  • Adapt treatment approaches to the patient's home environment, available space, equipment, functional abilities, and individual needs while following the established plan of care.
  • Coordinate care and communicate professionally with Physical Therapists, physicians, nurses, caregivers, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals as appropriate.
  • Communicate promptly regarding patient concerns, cancellations, scheduling changes, or other issues that may affect care.
  • Complete accurate, timely, and thorough documentation for daily treatment visits and other required clinical documentation.
  • Maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations, professional standards, payer requirements, PTA supervision requirements, and company policies.
  • Recognize changes in patient condition that may require notification of the supervising Physical Therapist, referring provider, or other healthcare professional.
  • Maintain patient confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.
  • Provide compassionate, respectful, and professional care to patients and their families in the home setting.


Requirements
  • Current and valid Physical Therapist Assistant license in good standing.
  • Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapist Assistant program.
  • Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, therapeutic exercise, and rehabilitation principles.
  • Strong understanding of physical therapy treatment techniques and functional mobility principles.
  • Ability to safely and effectively implement a Physical Therapist's established plan of care.
  • Knowledge of therapeutic exercise, gait training, balance training, functional mobility, neuromuscular re-education, strengthening, transfer training, and fall prevention.
  • Strong observation and patient monitoring skills.
  • Ability to recognize and appropriately communicate changes in patient condition or functional status.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively manage a mobile patient caseload while maintaining appropriate communication with the supervising Physical Therapist.
  • Must be punctual, dependable, organized, and professional.
  • Comfortable entering and providing care in patients' homes and working with patients and caregivers in a home-based environment.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation required.
  • Ability to travel throughout the assigned service area.
  • CPR/BLS certification preferred or required according to company policy.
  • Previous home health, mobile therapy, outpatient, orthopedic, neurological, geriatric, or community-based experience is preferred.


Mobile/Home-Based Care Expectations
Because this position involves providing care in patients' homes, the Physical Therapist Assistant must be able to:
  • Arrive at scheduled visits within the expected timeframe.
  • Manage travel time and maintain an efficient daily schedule.
  • Carry and transport necessary clinical equipment and supplies.
  • Adapt treatment approaches to different home environments and available space.
  • Maintain a safe and professional environment during every patient visit.
  • Communicate promptly regarding cancellations, scheduling changes, patient concerns, or changes in patient status.
  • Respect patients' homes, privacy, routines, and individual preferences.
  • Demonstrate sound clinical judgment within the PTA's scope of practice when working independently in the community.
  • Maintain appropriate communication with the supervising Physical Therapist regarding patient progress, concerns, and changes in condition.


Documentation and Compliance
The Physical Therapist Assistant is responsible for completing all required clinical documentation accurately and within established timeframes, including:
  • Daily treatment notes
  • Patient response to treatment
  • Progress toward established functional goals
  • Exercises and interventions performed
  • Patient and caregiver education
  • Home exercise program instruction and reinforcement
  • Communication with the supervising Physical Therapist
  • Documentation of changes in patient condition or functional status
  • Other documentation required by the organization, payer, supervising Physical Therapist, or applicable regulations


The PTA must practice within the scope of the California Physical Therapist Assistant license and applicable supervision requirements and must follow the established plan of care developed by the supervising Physical Therapist.

Job Type
Full-time – 1099 Independent Contractor

Pay Structure (1099)
  • Guaranteed base pay: $840 per week
  • Base compensation is calculated at $35 per patient visit, based on a minimum of 6 patient visits per day.
  • $35 per additional patient visit for visits beyond the daily base of 6.
  • Compensation is subject to the terms of the independent contractor agreement.
Schedule
4/10 Schedule
  • Four 10-hour workdays per week
  • Typical start time: 7:30 AM–8:30 AM, depending on patient scheduling and geographic coverage.
  • Daily schedule may vary based on patient locations, visit duration, and patient needs.


Work Location
Mobile/Home-Based – San Fernando Region

Ideal Candidate

title: Vice President, Tranformation Services - Denials Prevention
description:
Job Purpose
The Vice President, Transformation Services- Denials Prevention is responsible for leading enterprise-wide transformation strategies that prevent avoidable denials, protect revenue yield, and drive top-tier revenue cycle performance across health system clients. This role uses analytics, payer intelligence, operational assessments, and root-cause analysis to identify revenue leakage and translate findings into actionable changes across the revenue cycle.

The VP partners with client executives and internal operational, clinical, and analytics teams to move the organization from reactive denial recovery to proactive prevention, ensuring interventions are implemented at the point in the revenue cycle where the denial originates. Success is measured through sustainable reductions in preventable denials and write-offs, improved first-pass payment and clean claim performance, increased net revenue yield, and achievement of top-tier performance benchmarks.
Duties and Responsibilities

Lead enterprise-wide denial prevention strategy and transformation across hospital revenue cycle operations.
Identify and quantify opportunities to improve revenue yield by preventing avoidable revenue leakage before claims are submitted.
Analyze denial, write-off, payer, and reimbursement data to identify root causes, emerging trends, and high-value transformation opportunities.
Establish a comprehensive denial prevention framework that shifts organizational focus from denial recovery to upstream prevention and first-pass payment.
Develop prioritized transformation strategies based on financial impact, preventability, payer trends, operational performance, and implementation feasibility.
Drive performance toward top-tier industry benchmarks for initial denial rate, preventable denials, clean claim performance, denial write-offs, overturn rates, and first-pass payment.
Lead root-cause initiatives across Patient Access, Prior Authorization, Utilization Management, CDI, Coding, Revenue Integrity, Billing, Clinical Operations, and Payer Management.
Develop payer-specific prevention strategies addressing authorization, medical necessity, clinical validation, DRG downgrades, level of care, coding, timely filing, eligibility, and payment policy issues.
Identify emerging payer behavior and policy changes and proactively develop mitigation strategies before they materially impact revenue.
Partner with Managed Care and payer relations teams to identify systemic payer issues, contractual opportunities, and trends requiring payer escalation.
Define and monitor leading and lagging KPIs that measure both denial outcomes and the effectiveness of upstream prevention strategies.
Evaluate existing workflows and technology to identify opportunities to move edits and interventions earlier in the revenue cycle.
Quantify transformation outcomes including net new revenue, avoided revenue leakage, cash acceleration, reduced write-offs, and cost-to-collect improvement.
Partner with operational leaders to ensure transformation strategies are successfully implemented, adopted, measured, and sustained.
Develop standardized denial prevention methodologies, playbooks, benchmarks, and best practices that can be deployed consistently across clients.
Support client assessments, business development, and executive presentations by articulating denial prevention opportunities and expected financial value.
Foster an environment of continuous improvement, accountability, data-driven decision-making, and proactive revenue protection.

Qualifications

10 years of progressive leadership experience in Revenue Cycle Management and Denials work
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Finance, or a related field preferred
Proven experience in a leadership role within revenue cycle services, preferably in a healthcare hospital-based healthcare setting
Strong understanding of revenue cycle management principles and practices, with a demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality services to clients
Possess knowledge of state and federal governmental, legal, and regulatory provisions related to front-end, middle and backend revenue cycle operations
Excellent leadership skills, including the ability to motivate, mentor, and develop a high-performing team
Proficiency in revenue cycle management systems, electronic health records (EHR), and client management tools
Ability to adapt to a fast-paced and changing environment, managing multiple priorities and deadlines effectively
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
Strong interpersonal skills, ability to communicate well at all levels of the organization
Strong problem solving and creative skills and the ability to exercise sound judgment and make decisions based on accurate and timely analyses
High level of integrity and dependability with a strong sense of urgency and results oriented
Excellent written and verbal communication skills required

Working Conditions

Physical Demands: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to move around the work area; light lifting required; Sit; perform manual tasks; operate tools and other office equipment such as computer, computer peripherals and telephones; extend arms; kneel; talk and hear.
Mental Demands: The employee must be able to follow directions, collaborate with others, and handle stress.
Work Environment: The noise level in the work environment is usually minimal.

title: Substitute Classroom Aide
description:
SUMMARY OF PRIMARY FUNCTION
The Classroom Aide (Sub) is responsible for assisting the Classroom Staff in the implementation of a classroom program designed to give each child an opportunity to participate in experiences that will enrich his/her development in a safe environment. Classroom Aide Subs take the place of classroom staff absent for a period of time on an as needed basis, i.e.: illness, vacation or training. They also help recruit potential parents by providing information to them about the various program services and benefits offered to enrolled children and families.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Classroom Operations

Assists classroom staff with implementation of daily activities and classroom management principles.
Assist in implementing classroom activities around concepts that incorporate the interests of the classroom community and meet goals and objectives outlined in the Creative Curriculum.
Maintain enough flexibility to allow children’s interests to guide classroom direction.
Be responsible for and lead some activities as requested by the Teacher, Preschool Assistant Teacher or center leadership.
Establish and maintain positive, pleasant and trusting relationships with parents, respecting their individual needs and maintaining professional and appropriate boundaries.
Know all medical conditions/needs of the children in the classroom (including allergies) and how to respond to these needs.
Discuss what will be communicated to parents with the classroom team in order to give parents consistent messages in accordance with the Data Privacy policy.
Tends to children's personal hygiene needs, remaining especially attentive to them during routines such as diaper changing, cleaning, feeding, and changing soiled or wet clothes.
Assume other duties as requested by the classroom staff or center leadership.

Safety & Sanitation

Maintains a safe, clean, care-giving environment, practices good personal hygiene and hand washing, and assures the well-being and safety of all of the children in that environment.
Utilizes disciplinary measures appropriately as outlined in the Behavior Guidance Policies and Procedures.
Protects all children from physical punishment or verbal abuse by anyone in any program activity, and immediately reports any such incident to the person in charge.
Provides for the physical safety of each child from arrival time until departure time.
Assures that safety and sanitation policies and procedures are followed appropriately.
Assures that children are dressed appropriately for the weather and type of play in which they are engaged.
Assures that children are supervised at all times.
Have or obtain within 90 days of hire a First Aid and CPR Certification as well as maintain the certification during employment. Administers First Aid and/or CPR (if trained) when necessary.

Communication

Greets children and their parents warmly and with enthusiasm.
Maintains a cooperative attitude of working together with other staff, parents and volunteers in planning and implementing activities for the program/classroom.
Maintains a positive, calm attitude and a pleasant, soothing voice, and models this attitude and voice for parents and others working or volunteering in the program.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Must be at least 16 years of age; candidates strongly encouraged to obtain their high school diploma or GED.
Excellent communication skills.
Must enjoy and respect young children and their families.
Comfortable working with computers, willing and able to learn program specific systems.

title: Founding Operations Lead
description:
About the role

We’re looking for a Founding Operations Lead to build the connective tissue between our families, our product, and how Elayne operates.

At our stage, some of the most important things Elayne will eventually do in software still happen because a smart person figures them out manually. A family hits an edge case, an institution gives us a different answer than expected, a court rejects a filing. The process that worked ten times breaks on the eleventh.

Your job is to be close enough to the work to see those problems firsthand, rigorous enough to understand the pattern underneath them, and product-minded enough to help turn what we learn into systems that work for thousands of families.

You’ll move constantly between doing the work, designing the process, and helping build the product that makes the work disappear.

You’ll work directly with the CEO and across product and engineering. There is no established playbook to inherit. A large part of your job is creating it.

What you’ll own

  • The hardest operational problems: take ambiguous real-world issues from first signal to resolution, then turn what you learned into a better system
  • The manual-to-software loop: do new workflows by hand, identify what repeats, turn it into a durable process, then work with product and engineering to automate it
  • The operating system: build the SOPs, decision trees, escalation paths, quality standards, metrics, and internal tools that let Elayne handle more estates without simply adding more people
  • The voice of operational reality: make sure what families, attorneys, courts, and financial institutions are encountering makes its way into product decisions
  • The gaps between functions: own important problems that don’t fit neatly into one function and drive them across the finish line

Here’s what that can look like. A family thought they had found everything their dad left behind, but couldn’t be sure. We followed the trail manually, contacted institutions, pulled records, and eventually found over $100k in a forgotten retirement account. Then we mapped how we found it and turned that process into a system that has since surfaced millions of dollars families didn’t know were there.

That loop is the job. Solve the problem once because a family needs you to. Build the system so the next thousand don’t.

Who we’re looking for

  • You’ve built from zero to one. You’ve worked at an early-stage company where important things were undefined, personally owned messy problems, and created structure instead of waiting for it
  • You’re an unusually strong operator. You can take a messy problem with incomplete or conflicting information, figure out what is actually happening, and drive it to resolution
  • You think in systems. When something happens repeatedly, your instinct is to find the pattern, define the decision points, measure it, and make the process better
  • You’re product-minded without needing to be the product manager. You can translate operational reality into clear requirements, distinguish what should stay human from what software should absorb, and work exceptionally well with product and engineering
  • You have judgment and warmth. You can earn trust from someone dealing with grief, money, family dynamics, or bureaucracy without losing clarity, boundaries, or speed
  • No work is beneath you. You’re as comfortable calling an institution, investigating a strange edge case, or fixing a broken workflow as you are designing the system that eventually replaces that work

We care more about the shape of your experience than the exact title. You might come from early-stage operations, product operations, fintech, healthcare, insurance, legaltech, trust and safety, or have been a founder yourself. What matters is that you’ve personally turned messy real-world work into systems that scale.

How we work

We’re small, fast, and close to the people using what we build. The distance between discovering a problem and changing the product is intentionally short.

Everyone here owns outcomes, not tickets. We communicate directly, move quickly, and care deeply about impact and getting the details right.

Location & compensation

NoMad, NYC office

$140,000 to $180,000 + meaningful equity

Medical, dental, and vision insurance + 401(k)

Equal opportunity

Elayne is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants based on ability, experience, and potential, and do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic under applicable federal, state, or local laws.

title: IT/OT Engineer
description:
Position: IT/OT Engineer. Location: Cork, Ireland.
PACIV, a global leader in industrial automation solutions with offices in Ireland, the United States and Puerto Rico, and serving the Life Science, Food & Beverage (F&B) and Utilities industries, is looking for an experienced IT/OT Engineer for a F&B project. This is a site-based role.
The IT/OT Engineer will report to the IT/OT Automation Lead and is responsible for delivering the technical design, implementation, commissioning, and documentation of all IT and OT network infrastructure supporting the new plant. This includes site network architecture, segmentation, DMZ layers, firewalls, server/virtualization environments, industrial Ethernet, and secure connectivity between PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, MES and business systems.
Act as the technical owner of network and architectural decisions during project execution, ensuring all systems are delivered safely, on time, and in full, meeting the Company’s global IT/OT, cybersecurity and engineering standards. Your expertise will be essential to ensuring the facility is operationally ready, cyber secure, and scalable for future digitalisation as the site progresses to start‑up.
As part of the plant project team, you will play an important role in technical execution, commissioning readiness, documentation, and troubleshooting during start‑up. This role provides an excellent pathway for internal development into broader engineering, IT/OT or operations leadership positions within the Company.

Responsibilities of the Role
Project Execution & Commissioning
  • Lead the installation, configuration, integration, and commissioning of network components and server/virtualization environments.
  • Conduct FAT/SAT for network equipment, cybersecurity controls, and OT system connectivity.
  • Troubleshoot network and IT/OT connectivity issues during construction, commissioning, and start‑up.

Technical Ownership – Network & Architecture
  • Act as the technical Subject Matter Expert for IT/OT network infrastructure, including LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, industrial Ethernet, VLANs, segmentation, DMZ and firewall architecture.
  • Define and validate the IT/OT network topology supporting PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, MES, historians, and business systems.
  • Ensure alignment to Company global IT/OT standards and cybersecurity requirements.

Cybersecurity & Compliance
  • Implement cybersecurity controls across IT/OT systems, including segmentation, access control, hardening, patching, backup/restore, and secure remote access.
  • Support cybersecurity assessments, remediation plans, and compliance documentation.
  • Maintain audit‑ready technical records for all network and OT infrastructure.

Cross‑Functional Collaboration
  • Work closely with Automation, Engineering, Operations, Quality, R&I, EHS, and Supply Chain to ensure network readiness for commissioning and start‑up.
  • Act as the primary technical interface for network‑related topics with EPCM partners, integrators, Global/Regional IT/OT, and automation/MES vendors.

Infrastructure Delivery & Support
  • Support deployment of virtual machines, storage, domain integration, user profiles, and IT/OT monitoring tools.
  • Ensure stable and secure connectivity for control systems, SCADA/MES, historian, and digital quality solutions.
  • Provide hands‑on technical support during system bring‑up, line trials, and early operations.

Documentation & Standards
  • Develop and maintain network documentation: architecture diagrams, IP schemas, firewall rulebooks, switch configurations, OT device registers, and validation protocols.
  • Ensure EPCM and vendors deliver all required documentation for commissioning and operations handover.

Operational Readiness & Handover
  • Support creation of IT/OT SOPs, troubleshooting guides, backup/restore procedures, PM plans, and CMMS master data.
  • Ensure all infrastructure is validated, backed up, and documented prior to handover to Operations/IT.



Reporting & Decision Support
  • Provide status reporting on network and IT/OT readiness, risks, and open issues to the IT/OT Lead – Automation and project leadership.
  • Offer technical insights to support design, commissioning, and operational decisions.

Requirements

Candidates must have a valid EU Work Permit and Irish residency
Please no agencies

Qualifications
  • BSc in Software Engineering, Automation/Control Engineering, Electronic/Network Engineering or related field.

Experience/Skills Required
  • 4+ years of experience in IT/OT, network engineering or industrial systems integration.
  • Experience in manufacturing, F&B, pharmaceutical, or related process environments preferred.
  • Experience in IT/OT network design (LAN, VLAN, WiFi), industrial Ethernet, cybersecurity, and automation system connectivity.
  • Familiarity with PLC, SCADA, HMI systems and OT connectivity requirements.
  • Experience collaborating with engineering, automation vendors, operations, IT and cross‑functional engineering teams.
  • Experience with Cisco, Fortinet, HP, Stratix switches, firewalls, and network tools.
  • Knowledge of IT/OT convergence, integrating business systems with automation layers.
  • Experience with virtual servers/VMs (VMware/Hyper‑V/Nutanix), backups, and resilience.
  • Ability to interpret network diagrams, specifications, and infrastructure documentation.
  • Troubleshooting experience in IT/OT connectivity, SCADA/MES links, and device networks.
  • Familiarity with project execution processes (FAT/SAT, commissioning, documentation).

title: System Test Specialist
description:
Systel Careers – Test Evaluation System Specialist – Sugar Land, TX

We are seeking a dynamic System Test Specialist to join our team at Systel. You will join the Systems Test Team at Systel, which is responsible for completing tests and validation of the first article Engineering units as well as providing support to multiple departments in the organization. This critical role ensures that our rugged computer solutions meet the rigorous standards required to reliably perform mission-critical operations in harsh environments.
This position is full-time onsite (in-person) at our headquarters in Sugar Land, TX. Please note that some travel may be required.

Who You Are

You are a detail‑oriented, self‑motivated technical professional with strong hands‑on experience in computer electronics and system‑level testing. You excel in environments that require precision, adaptability, and clear communication. You are comfortable working collaboratively across engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams and can manage shifting priorities without losing focus. You bring a solid understanding of hardware and software interactions, and you’re able to interpret engineering schematics, wiring diagrams, and component‑level documentation with confidence. You value continuous improvement and actively contribute to advancing processes, tools, and test methodologies.

Responsibilities
  • Execute automated and manual test procedures on integrated hardware and software systems.
  • Set up, configure, and verify test environments including operating systems, BIOS settings, drivers, networks, and peripheral hardware.
  • Perform hardware diagnostics at the board and component level using schematics, diagrams, test fixtures, and electronic measurement tools.
  • Analyze system performance data, identify deviations, and produce clear, detailed reports covering results, anomalies, and corrective recommendations.
  • Document and track defects in hardware and software using systems such as JIRA.
  • Verify compliance with internal specifications, industry standards, and ruggedization/military requirement guidelines.
  • Conduct root cause analysis of failed units and collaborate with hardware, software, and manufacturing engineers on corrective actions and retest activities.

Education and Experience
  • Associate’s degree in computer technology, electronics, or related discipline; equivalent technical experience considered.
  • 2–4 years of hands‑on experience in systems testing, computer hardware diagnostics, or related technical roles.
  • Proficiency with Windows and Linux environments, BIOS/UEFI configuration, hardware troubleshooting, and basic scripting (Python, shell, or similar).
  • Experience working with electronic components, PCB assemblies, and supporting documentation such as schematics and wiring diagrams.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and communication skills.
  • US Citizenship required.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Familiarity with industry standards and certifications relevant to rugged computing and military specifications.is desirable.
About Systel
Rugged Compute Where Mission Meets Critical.

Founded in 1988, Systel Inc.® is a leading manufacturer of rugged computer solutions with a relentless focus to support our customers and their missions. Our pedigree of capabilities spans numerous advanced platforms with thousands of successful deployments in the defense and commercial sectors. Systel’s rugged systems are designed and manufactured for continuous operation under the most extreme and austere environmental conditions. All our products are proudly made in the USA in our headquarters in Sugar Land, TX. We are AS9100:2016 and ISO 9001:2015 certified.

title: VP of Software Engineering
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a VP of Software Engineering based in the United States.

This is a high-impact executive leadership opportunity for an experienced software engineering leader to define and drive the technical vision of a fast-growing organization serving the defense and national security ecosystem. You will oversee software delivered under government contracts, internal platforms, and an enterprise-wide AI strategy. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving on the executive leadership team, you will shape technology direction while building and scaling the engineering organization. The role combines strategic ownership with hands-on decision-making across architecture, delivery, talent, AI adoption, and technology investment. You will work closely with executive leaders, government customers, operations, growth, finance, and cybersecurity teams. This is an opportunity to establish an engineering operating model, influence business growth, and build technology capabilities with meaningful mission impact.

Accountabilities

  • Lead, develop, and scale the software engineering organization, with accountability for delivery, quality, security, reliability, operational performance, and customer outcomes.
  • Define and implement an engineering operating model that evolves the organization from project-based execution toward outcome-based ownership, with clear intake, prioritization, metrics, and delivery rhythms.
  • Build a high-performing engineering team through strategic hiring, development, coaching, retention, and capability planning.
  • Establish engineering performance metrics and executive reporting covering delivery velocity, quality, AI adoption, operational effectiveness, and business impact.
  • Define and execute the organization-wide AI strategy, incorporating AI capabilities into customer products and internal workflows while driving measurable adoption.
  • Modernize how institutional knowledge is captured, organized, retrieved, and shared so expertise can scale across the organization.
  • Establish responsible AI governance across the software portfolio, including data handling, model selection and usage, evaluation practices, and coordination with IT and cybersecurity teams.
  • Own delivery of awarded government software contracts, including scope, schedule, technical quality, staffing, costs, utilization, and customer confidence.
  • Represent engineering and AI capabilities with government customers during delivery reviews, technical discussions, and business-development pursuits.
  • Partner with growth teams on federal software opportunities by shaping technical approaches, staffing models, pricing inputs, and delivery strategies.
  • Establish the technology strategy and architecture roadmap for customer-facing, internal, and field-deployed systems.
  • Own the internal platform supporting site teams, operations, members, and customer contracts, ensuring technology is deployed effectively and delivers measurable operational improvements.
  • Lead build-versus-buy decisions, vendor relationships, technology investments, and engineering portfolio prioritization.
  • Develop business cases for engineering investments, including headcount, tooling, platforms, and external vendors, and manage investments against agreed objectives.
  • Partner closely with executive leadership, product, operations, finance, growth, and IT/cybersecurity teams to align technology priorities with business and mission requirements.
  • Maintain strong technical relationships with government customers and external technology vendors and partners.
  • Drive continuous improvement in engineering delivery, AI adoption, operational workflows, and organizational scalability.

    • Requirements

    • 8+ years of software engineering experience with progressive leadership responsibility, including ownership of a full engineering organization or software product function.
    • Demonstrated experience leading software delivery for U.S. government customers, with an understanding of federal procurement, delivery, security, compliance, and operational constraints.
    • Strong command of modern AI practices, including large language models (LLMs), agentic frameworks, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), orchestration, evaluation, and AI governance.
    • Proven experience building and scaling engineering organizations, including defining operating models, hiring teams, developing talent, and transitioning toward outcome-based delivery.
    • Experience owning delivery economics, including cost, staffing, utilization, financial performance, and business cases for technology investment.
    • Demonstrated ability to manage executive-level customer and cross-functional relationships and communicate complex technical strategies clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
    • Experience setting technology strategy, architecture direction, engineering priorities, and investment roadmaps.
    • Strong business judgment and the ability to make high-quality decisions in ambiguous, rapidly changing environments.
    • Excellent leadership, communication, problem-solving, prioritization, and organizational skills, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
    • Preferred experience in defense, national security, or another highly regulated environment involving security clearances, compliance requirements, or controlled data.
    • Preferred experience contributing to federal software capture, including technical approaches, staffing strategies, and cost inputs for government proposals.
    • Preferred experience delivering software used by field-based or operational teams.
    • An active U.S. government security clearance is preferred.
    • Must be authorized to work in the United States and eligible and willing to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance as a condition of employment.

      • Benefits

      • Competitive base salary range of $230,000–$275,000 USD, depending on qualifications and experience.
      • Executive-level opportunity with direct exposure to company leadership and significant influence over technology and business strategy.
      • Remote work environment within the United States.
      • Opportunity to build and scale an engineering organization and establish its operating model.
      • Ownership of an enterprise-wide AI strategy with meaningful influence on both products and internal operations.
      • Opportunity to work directly with government and national security customers on mission-critical technology.
      • Significant visibility into business growth, technology investment, customer engagement, and strategic decision-making.
      • Opportunity to shape the technology roadmap, engineering culture, hiring strategy, and long-term organizational capabilities.

title: Lead Product Engineer (Irvine) - On-Site
description:
Eggs Unlimited is one of the world's largest suppliers of eggs, servicing the biggest retail and food manufacturing companies around the globe. Every day, we find homes for millions of eggs by tapping into our vast supply chain and customer networks. Bringing sellers and buyers together in fair market negotiations, we open up a world of possibilities for expanding their knowledge, reach, and access. With dedicated service teams and a mission to uphold transparency and trustworthiness, we create quick and creative solutions to help manage the ever-evolving demands of the global egg industry.

The Role

We leverage AI to bring food to every table.

You are a hands-on product engineer embedded with operations. You find the workflow problems worth solving, build and run the software that solves them, and own whether the business actually adopts it. AI-assisted development is how the work gets done. Human judgment, controls, and production quality are not negotiable.

The Problem We Are Solving

We are building the intelligent operating platform behind a global food supply chain, combining leading models, our own operational data and business rules, and the judgment of the people who trade for a living.

Extracting an order from an email is no longer the hard part. The loop is. Forecast where the market is going, project demand forward by customer and by product, and know what we are long and short on any given day. Then decide what to buy and what to sell, build the load, and book the freight against a computed view of what that lane is actually worth. Trading, supply, freight, and the ledger stop being separate systems stitched together by a spreadsheet and become one connected flow, with a named person accountable at every point where money moves.

The product layer is largely greenfield. You will be building it, not maintaining someone else's version of it, though it has to work with the operational systems the business already runs on. We move quickly and we build practical solutions that scale, not demos.

The Orchestrator

The person in this seat does not write a specification and wait. They take an idea, direct a fleet of agents at it, and produce a working implementation themselves, at a volume of output that would not have been possible from one person two years ago. If your monthly token consumption would look alarming to a traditional engineering manager, you are probably working the way we work. What we measure is not the volume: it is whether you decompose work well, keep context under control, catch the plausible and wrong answer, and stand behind what ships.

You do not need prior experience in our exact stack. What matters is whether you can build things, whether you take ownership, and whether you can hold the big picture while you do it. Think like a customer, act like an owner.

This seat pairs that with a product management background. You will sit with the traders, the purchasing coordinators, and the logistics desks, work out what the job is underneath the spreadsheet, and then own both halves: the discovery that finds the right manual burden to remove, and the delivery and adoption that make it stick. The goal is not to strip work out for its own sake, but to remove the burden while preserving the human judgment the business depends on.

What You Will Own

Discovery at the Desk: Observe the workflow first, then interview operators to validate what you saw. Identify the work that can be safely automated, and the work that must stay under human judgment.

Agent Orchestration: Decompose a problem into work that can run in parallel, direct agents at it, control context, reconcile conflicting output, test what comes back, and remain responsible for the final system. This is an operating capability, not a tool preference.

Build and Ship It: Own the path from a validated need to monitored production. The platform team supplies tooling, guardrails, CI/CD, evaluation infrastructure, and architecture and peer review.

Implementation Across the Company: Your responsibility continues past the merge. Partner with operators and their managers on rollout, training, feedback, and iteration, and stay accountable for whether adoption is real rather than announced.

Adoption Discipline: Every release should remove more operational burden than it adds, use the channels operators already work in, need almost no instruction to adopt, and fail safely and visibly.

Backlog and Sequencing: Own the backlog for your domain and the order of work, co-owned with the business leaders whose desks are affected, with the tradeoffs written down.

Measurement in Operator Currency: Define done in the operators' own terms, hours saved, loads moved, claims recovered, follow-ups caught, against a baseline you established first. Report honestly on how often the system is right, how often it is wrong and in which direction, and how often it escalates to a person.

Engineering Standards: Ship maintainable, tested, observable, secure systems, with explicit evaluations, audit trails, rollback paths, and safe failure modes. Agent-generated work is held to the same production standard as anything you type.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days:

  • You know how at least two desks actually work, from sitting with them rather than from a document.

  • One workflow problem chosen, with the baseline measured before anything is built.

  • Something small in production that an operator uses by choice.

In your first six months:

  • One desk workflow measurably lighter: a documented baseline, a named operator owner, a measured reduction in manual work, and agreed behavior when it fails.

  • A working evaluation and measurement layer for what you shipped: how often it is right, how often it is wrong, in which direction, and how often it hands back to a person.

  • A prioritized backlog co-owned with business leaders, with sequence, tradeoffs, owners, and expected outcomes made explicit.

In your first year:

  • Production automation live across more than one operational function, each piece with a named owner, monitoring, rollback, an audit trail, and a stop path the desk itself controls.

  • Adoption you can prove in operator currency: hours saved, loads moved, claims recovered, follow-ups caught, errors avoided.

The clearest sign that you are succeeding: operators bring you the next workflow, because the last one made their work better.

What You Bring

  • Demonstrated experience with product discovery, requirements synthesis, and prioritization in real operating environments.

  • You ship production code. You are accountable for what it does in production, however it was produced.

  • Serious agentic development practice. Show us real parallel-agent work: how you decompose tasks, manage context, review and reconcile output, design tests and evaluations, an example of a failure you caught, and a case where you decided not to use an agent. Anonymize anything confidential.

  • Ownership. You have carried something end to end and been accountable for whether it worked, not for whether it shipped.

  • Enough backend, data, and deployment competence to design APIs and data models, integrate systems, deploy and instrument services, and debug production issues independently, while working with platform, security, and domain experts where it matters.

  • Judgment about correctness in nondeterministic systems: evaluations, observability, failure-mode thinking, guardrails, human escalation, and rollback.

  • You can make technical decisions and tradeoffs understandable to people who are not engineers, document them clearly, and take operator feedback on board.

  • Experience building within messy operational reality, email, spreadsheets, chat threads, and phone calls, rather than replacing it with something tidier that operators will not adopt.

We do not screen on years of experience, and we do not screen on which technologies you have used. Seniority here is calibrated by scope, judgment, autonomy, and outcomes. Show us what you have built.

Helpful Experience

  • Food distribution, logistics, retail and CPG, trading, ERP or EDI, financial operations, or other trading-partner ecosystems.

  • Ambiguous, high-ownership environments where defining and building were tightly coupled, for example as a founder, early employee, product engineer, or forward-deployed engineer.

Team, Environment, and How Decisions Get Made

You report to the Director of Technology and join a small, senior engineering team. This is a lead role in scope and judgment, not in headcount: it does not manage people. The platform engineering lead sets the engineering and evaluation bar, owns shared tooling and guardrails, and is the second reviewer on your work. Infrastructure, identity, and access control sit with the platform team. Priorities are agreed with the Director of Technology and the business leaders who own the affected desks.

Our environment spans cloud services on Azure, relational and event-sourced data stores, services in Go and Python, a TypeScript front end, an enterprise ERP core, and a retrieval layer over the company's own operating history. You will not be expected to have used all of it.

Why Eggs Unlimited

  • Join at the "second floor" of a hyper-growth company rapidly becoming a skyscraper – help build what comes next.

  • Outsized impact opportunity – building people, leadership, culture, & support continued expansion.

  • Access meaningful advancement opportunities as the company continues to expand.

  • Modern hardware and access to leading models and development tools, with clear security and data-handling guardrails rather than blanket tool bans.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Base Salary: $180,000 - $210,000+ annually

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Company-paid life and disability insurance.

  • 401(k) plan with company match.

  • Generous PTO accruals, increasing each year.

  • Free daily lunch, snacks, and refreshments.

title: Data Integration Engineer I
description:
Job Summary
We are seeking a curious and detail-oriented Data Engineer to join our Data Operations team. In this role, you will help build, operate, and improve the healthcare data pipelines that power our analytics and AI platforms. You will collaborate with engineers, analysts, and implementation teams to ensure data is accurately ingested, processed, and delivered across the organization.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone early in their data engineering career who enjoys working with complex real-world data and is eager to grow their skills in modern data platforms within a healthcare technology environment.

Duties & Responsibilities

Monitor and support the daily operation of production data pipelines to ensure successful data processing and workflow execution.
Troubleshoot pipeline failures and assist in resolving data processing issues, escalating complex problems when necessary.
Investigate and help resolve data quality issues, anomalies, and discrepancies, particularly within healthcare datasets.
Perform data validation and testing to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency of integrated data.
Analyze datasets to identify patterns, irregularities, and potential data issues, supporting proactive data quality improvements.
Collaborate with implementation teams to understand client data formats and integration requirements.
Assist with data reconciliation and validation during client onboarding and integration processes.
Write and optimize SQL queries to support data transformations, validation, and analysis tasks.
Assist in the development, testing, and maintenance of data integration pipelines.
Create and maintain documentation for data workflows, pipeline behavior, and operational procedures.
Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback to improve code quality and development practices.

Technology Stack
We are mid-migration to a modern data platform. You’ll work across both environments and contribute to the transition.

Current Environment

SQL Server
Python · PowerShell
Jenkins

Target Platform

Snowflake
Astronomer / Apache Airflow
Python-based pipelines

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proficiency in SQL and experience working with relational databases, including writing queries for data analysis and transformation.
Experience with scripting or automation using Python or a comparable programming language to support data processing or integration tasks.
Familiarity with ETL/ELT concepts and data pipeline fundamentals, including data ingestion, transformation, and validation processes.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate data issues and identify root causes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with healthcare data, including Medicare, Medicaid, or medical claims datasets.
Familiarity with common healthcare code sets, such as ICD, CPT, or HCPCS.
Exposure to modern data platforms and tools, such as Snowflake, Apache Airflow, or cloud-based data environments.
Familiarity with CI/CD practices or tools, such as Jenkins or GitHub Actions.
Understanding of data warehousing concepts, including dimensional modeling and analytics-oriented data structures.

Why Join Us
You will have the opportunity to work on modern data platforms and tools, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and help build reliable data systems that drive meaningful insights and business value.

Meaningful work with direct impact on healthcare outcomes
Remote-friendly environment
Opportunities for professional growth and skill development
Comprehensive healthcare coverage

*Please note, due to the requirements of this position, responses may automatically disqualify you from moving forward in the application process. Please review minimum qualifications thoroughly before applying.

description:

title: DevOps Engineer (AWS / Terraform)
description:
DevOps Engineer (AWS / Terraform)


🚀 Lokalizacja: Warszawa, Wola - blisko stacji metra.

🛠 Technologie: AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Java ecosystem

Projekt: Budowa od zera nowej infrastruktury AWS i migracja dwóch kluczowych aplikacji.

On-call: Brak


O stanowisku

Poszukujemy doświadczonego DevOps Engineera, który dołączy do projektu obejmującego budowę nowego środowiska AWS dla dwóch aplikacji oraz migrację z istniejącej infrastruktury chmurowej. Osoba na tym stanowisku będzie odpowiedzialna za rozwój i utrzymanie infrastruktury jako kodu, automatyzację procesów deploymentu oraz współpracę z zespołami developerskimi i operacyjnymi w celu zapewnienia stabilności, bezpieczeństwa i skalowalności środowiska.

Stanowisko jest przypisane do biura w Warszawie.


Zakres obowiązków

  • Tworzenie, rozwijanie i utrzymywanie infrastruktury jako kodu (Infrastructure as Code) dla różnych środowisk.
  • Rozwijanie oraz utrzymywanie konfiguracji jako kodu wspierającej pełny proces dostarczania usług.
  • Współpraca z zespołami developerskimi i operacyjnymi w celu zapewnienia płynnych wdrożeń oraz skalowalności aplikacji.
  • Budowanie i utrzymywanie pipeline’ów CI/CD.
  • Monitorowanie wydajności systemów oraz rozwiązywanie problemów związanych z dostępnością i niezawodnością środowisk.
  • Wdrażanie nowych technologii i usprawnień wspierających kulturę ciągłego doskonalenia.
  • Udział w projektowaniu i implementacji mechanizmów bezpieczeństwa chroniących dane i infrastrukturę.
  • Wsparcie migracji aplikacji do nowego środowiska AWS.


Wymagania

  • Minimum 3 lata doświadczenia na stanowisku DevOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer lub podobnym.
  • Bardzo dobra znajomość AWS oraz praktyczne doświadczenie z Terraform.
  • Doświadczenie w pracy z konteneryzacją i orkiestracją (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Znajomość narzędzi CI/CD oraz automatyzacji, takich jak Jenkins, Ansible czy Terraform.
  • Dobra znajomość systemów Linux/Unix.
  • Umiejętność skryptowania w Bash, Python, Groovy lub Go.
  • Doświadczenie we współpracy z zespołami developerskimi pracującymi głównie w technologii Java.
  • Umiejętność analitycznego myślenia i rozwiązywania problemów.
  • Komunikatywność i umiejętność pracy zespołowej.
  • Wykształcenie wyższe techniczne (informatyka, inżynieria lub pokrewne).
  • Bardzo dobra znajomość języka angielskiego.


Mile widziane

  • Certyfikacje AWS lub inne certyfikaty chmurowe / DevOps.
  • Doświadczenie z narzędziami monitoringu i log managementu (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack).
  • Znajomość zagadnień związanych z architekturą sieciową oraz security best practices.
  • Doświadczenie z administracją bazami danych SQL/NoSQL i optymalizacją wydajności.
  • Doświadczenie pracy w środowisku regulowanym (np. PCI).
  • Znajomość GCP lub Azure.

title: Manufacturing Engineering Program Manager-Aircraft Lighting
description:
The Aerospace Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) organization is responsible to partner with Engineering, Program Management and Integrated Supply Chain (Operations/factory) to drive New Product Development (NPD) initiatives into Aerospace lighting products.


This position will work with design engineering on new product designs in the field of aircraft lighting to ensure the product meets design to cost and design for manufacturability and testability targets prior to entry into full production.

Product must also meet the required manufacturing level at each of the Integrated Product Delivery System (IPDS) Phase Exit reviews.

The position works closely with Sourcing to ensure that suppliers are ready for production. Additionally, the successful candidate will identify and track capital, develop manufacturing and capacity plans, prepare trade studies, maintain NPD scorecards, plan and support development builds in the factory and at sub-tier suppliers, lead failure analysis and problem resolution teams, identify manufacturing risks and develop risk reduction plans.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills are required to prepare data and presentations and present to customers and management. Excellent leadership skills are required to influence and drive other functions to achieve results. Multi-tasking, organization and project management skills required.

Reports directly to the AME NPD Engineering Manager and indirectly to the program manager on the project.

*Requires a bachelor’s degree in engineering. Masters degree preferred.
*Min. of 2 years of experience in project engineering and/or manufacturing engineering preferred.
*Computer skills such as PowerPoint, Excel, Access and scheduling tolls required.
